title: Form 8606: the form that does the work
audience: Anyone who has done a Roth conversion or backdoor Roth without filing Form 8606
thesis: Form 8606 is the IRS form that tracks your non-deductible IRA contributions and Roth conversions year by year. Skip it and the IRS assumes every dollar in your Roth is earnings — and taxes every withdrawal.

concepts.label: What Form 8606 does
concepts.body: Form 8606 Part I tracks non-deductible traditional IRA contributions. Part II tracks Roth conversions. Without Part II, the IRS has no record of the year-by-year basis — and reverts to assuming every dollar in the Roth is pre-tax earnings.

concepts.label: The cost of skipping it
concepts.body: Skip Form 8606 for a $7,500 backdoor Roth conversion — and 30 years later, when you withdraw $400,000, the IRS treats the entire amount as taxable. Tax at 24%: $96,000 owed. The form costs nothing; the cost of skipping it is six figures.

concepts.label: When to file
concepts.body: File Form 8606 every year you do a non-deductible traditional IRA contribution or a Roth conversion. Attach it to your Form 1040. You can amend prior years with Form 8606 + 1040-X — there's no statute of limitations on tracking your own basis.
